# Conclusion

This paper analyzed 72,856 real charging sessions to develop a data-driven V2G scheduling system. Key finding, only 5.1% of sessions are V2G eligible, but targeted engagement could increase this to 12%. The 17:00-20:00 window represents optimal alignment between grid needs and user availability.

Integration with EVerest demonstrates real-time feasibility, with <1 second decision latency. Revenue potential ranges from $0.47/user/year (conservative) to $1.31/user/year (optimistic), with scale projections showing fleet level potential.

While challenges remain, particularly the low basline availability and narrow temporal window, data-driven targeting strategies show promise for improving V2G participation. As EV adoption rate goes higher, such systems will be essential for maximizing vehicle-grid integration value while maintaining user satisfaction.


## Future Work
Machine learing could learn individual user patterns over time, allowing personalized scheduling. Battery degradation modeling would help optimize V2G participation while preserving battery health. Expanding temporal windows through weekend and seasonal analysis could identify additional opportunities.
